full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: Pre-emptee Md Mofizul Islam Sarkar seeks review of the Judgment dated January 13, 2002 recorded by this Court in Civil Revision No. 3535 of 1999 springing out of a Pre-emption proceeding under section 96 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (for short The Act) on presentation of Review Petition whereupon Rule was issued calling upon Pre-emptor-opposite party Subitri Sundari Mali to show cause as to why Judgment dated 13-1-2002 passed by Division Bench in Civil Revision No. 3535 of 1999 should not be reviewed or such other order or further order or orders be not passed which this Court might deem fit and proper. 

 8. Substituted opposite party Nos. 1(a) to 1(c) entered appearance in Civil Rule and filed an Affidavit-in-opposition. In the Affidavit-in-opposition statements made are: 

 15. In Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case in paragraph 5 of the petition it is stated that Netai Mali had been owner of Eight annas thirteen gondas one kara and one kranti (।। ১৩√ক্রান্তি) and Netai Mali died leaving behind four (4) daughters, namely, Subitri Sundari Mali (Pre-emptor), Pulini Sundari Mali, Giribala Mali and Usha Rani Mali. In paragraph 6 it is stated that Pulini Sundari. Giribala and Usha Rani Mali by way of seven (7) separate deeds of conveyance transferred their all interest in favour of Subitri Sundari Mali (Pre-emptor). 

 20. In Chandra Kumar Maladas vs Abdul Motaleb and others (Supra) purchase by respondent No. 1 Abdul Motaleb from Manmohan Parsana and Rajani had been pre-empted by other co-sharer holders and, as such, Pre-emptor had no subsisting interest in the holding to pre-empt the auction sale in favour of respondent No. 2. It has been laid down: A Pre-emptor must not only have a subsisting interest in the holding when he filed the application for pre-emption under section 26F of The Bengal Tenancy Act, but must continue to hold the self-same interest to the date when the case is finally disposed of. It has, also, been held: A co-sharer means a person whose interest subsists throughout the course of the application to pre-empt and not a person who held such an interest in the beginning, but lost it before its disposal. Equally, a fresh interest acquired at a latter stage cannot be tacked on to the interest held in the beginning but lost during the pendency of the application. 

 23. "Proceeding" is a term of wide amplitude. "Proceeding" is a prescribed course of action for enforcement of a legal right. The word "proceeding" has been stated in the Black's Law Dictionary, Sixth Edition page 1204 in the following way: 

 "An act which is done by the authority or direction of the court, agency, or tribunal, express or implied; an act necessary to be done in order to obtain a given end; a prescribed mode of action for carrying into effect a legal right. All the steps or measures adopted in the prosecution or defence of an action. Statter vs United States, CCA Alaska, 66 F 2d 819, 822. The word may be used synonymously with "action" or "suit" to describe the entire course of an action at law or suit in equity from the issuance of the writ or filing of the complaint until the entry of a final judgment, or may be used to describe any act done by authority of a court of law and every step required to be taken in any cause by either party. The proceedings of a suit embrace all matters that occur in its progress judicially. 

 24. The word “proceeding" what it connotes, came up before Full Bench of Madhya Pradesh High Court in Ratanchand Darbarilal Saina and others vs Rajendra Kumar Khoobchand and others, AIR 1970 MP 1(4) FB wherein it has been stated that a suit, appeal or second appeal can all be described as proceeding.
